anchor.quote: $B_0$ is the second contraction, a linear map from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors

anchor.note: The page introduces v only as a generic length-t vector. The earlier binding on radix-digit-convolution makes v the second integer, a different object, so the reader cannot tell what v denotes here.
The constant pi, covered by the complex-numbers and roots-of-unity basics (roots of unity are written with e^{2 pi i/q}).
Exponential notation e^x, covered by the complex-numbers basics.
Norm notation for the operator norm of a linear map, a known concept; the symbol is not part of that concept's name, so this is the standard notation the reader is taught with it.

gaps.note: An integral of a Gaussian function. It is not in the reader profile, and the page neither explains it nor links it.

gaps.quote: a unimodal function summed over the integers is at most its integral plus its maximum
gaps.note: Not a profile concept, and the page neither defines it nor links it.
Needs the Gaussian integral value and the comparison of a unimodal sum with its integral plus maximum, neither of which the reader can check. The bound on the norm of S' rests on it.

gaps.quote: the factor $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$ in $D$ cancels the Gaussian factor of $T$ at $\ell_j$
gaps.note: The page never gives the weights of T or the expansion of (Nu)_j, so the cancellation and the claim that the j-th summand is exactly u_j cannot be checked.
Attributed to prior work without the (cited) marker. The page does not state what hypotheses the estimate needs or why it applies here, beyond saying it is the same estimate.

gaps.quote: So the Neumann series $\sum_{i\ge 0}(I-N)^i$, the matrix analogue of the geometric series, converges to $N^{-1}$
gaps.note: Convergence of the series and identification of its sum with the inverse of N are presented as following from the bound on ||I-N|| but are not proved or cited, and the reader cannot check them from the page.
Needs the triangle inequality and submultiplicativity of the operator norm, which the page does not state.

gaps.quote: The operator norm for the maximum-modulus vector norm is the largest absolute row sum, so $\|C\|=1$.
gaps.note: The formula for the operator norm under the maximum-modulus vector norm is stated without proof or citation, and the reader's known operator-norm concept does not include it.
The page says both maps are contractions but does not show the norm of B_0 is at most one, nor why contractivity makes these the maps A and B_0. The choice is asserted, not derived.
